key_insight: BRIDGE turns routinely measured geotechnical index properties into a calibrated surrogate that predicts mechanical property ranges while preserving constitutive-model consistency.
engineering_relevance: It reduces the need for expensive laboratory testing by leveraging sparse calibrations to estimate soil behavior for many samples in practical design workflows.
method: Screen the dataset for outliers and non-physical responses.
Partition retained samples into Cells based on basic properties and select a small calibration subset from each Cell.
Calibrate an Extended Cam-Clay FEM model for each selected sample and use the converged calibrations to define a Cell-level surrogate and predictive envelope.
evidence_signal: On the Tokyo-CLAY/14/67760 database, the framework predicts an entire Cell from only 10–20% of its samples used for calibration.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen mechanical model, binning rules, and sampling strategy, so poor Cell definitions or domain shift may reduce reliability.
paper_title: BRIDGE: Bridging Routine Inputs and Digital modelling for Geotechnical Engineering
